papers.title: Don't Drop Dropout: Optimizing Layer Sparsity for Efficient LLM Training and Inference
papers.abstract: Layer dropout (a.k.a. stochastic depth) has been shown to enable faster training, higher accuracy, and robustness to zero-shot layer pruning in both language and vision transformers. However, as models and datasets have scaled, dropout - particularly layer dropout - has largely disappeared from large language models (LLMs) pre-training recipes. While some prior work has reported that dropout can degrade accuracy, no comprehensive study has quantified, let alone mitigated, this effect. In this study, we show that layer dropout should be used in state-of-the-art LLM training, establishing best practices and scaling analysis for both training and post-training benefits. Concretely, with optimal layer distribution, time schedule, and optimizer hyperparameters, we observe that at the same training FLOPs layer dropout leads to lower loss. For a given number of training steps, LLMs can achieve lower or similar validation loss while saving upto 25% of training FLOPs. Moreover, layer dropout enables significant post-training optimizations, such as early exit, intermediate-layer skipping, and self-speculative decoding, yielding up to 1.5x inference speedup with negligible accuracy loss. Across more than 2400 training experiments, spanning models from 271M to 8.2B parameters and datasets up to 160B tokens, we demonstrate that these findings extend reliably to large-scale training regimes. All pre-training experiments were run on Cerebras CS-3 systems.
papers.comment: This is a slightly extended version of the paper published at ICML 2026
papers.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2026)

summary.takeaway: 最佳配置的 layer dropout 可将训练 FLOPs 降低最多 25%，同时保持或提升 validation loss，并实现最高 1.5 倍的推理加速。
summary.method: 作者系统性地调节 layer‑wise dropout 率、时间调度、优化器超参数以及粒度（per‑sequence 与 per‑batch），覆盖多种模型规模。
summary.why_for_you: 本研究提供高效的训练技术和 loss‑landscape 见解，对 adversarial training 与可信 LLM 部署具有参考价值。

summary.limitations: 动态 early‑exit、更广硬件平台以及 sub‑layer dropout 表现不佳的原因留待后续研究。

deep_dive.overview: 本文对 decoder‑only LLM 的 stochastic depth（layer dropout）进行大规模实证研究，覆盖 271M‑8.2B 参数模型及最高 160B token。通过联合优化跨深度的 dropout 分布、训练步骤的递减 schedule 以及匹配的 optimizer 设置，实现显著计算节省，并支持 zero‑shot 推理优化，如 early exit、intermediate‑layer skipping 与 self‑speculative decoding。分析还比较了 per‑batch 与 per‑sequence dropout 粒度，并对比了 layer dropout 与 sub‑layer dropout。

methodology.title: 超参数搜索
methodology.detail: 系统地调整 dropout 率、depth‑wise 分布和 temporal 调度，同时在 20 tokens‑per‑parameter 的计算最优预算下调优 optimizer 超参数。

methodology.title: 粒度比较
methodology.detail: 实现并评估 per‑batch（所有序列使用相同 mask）和 per‑sequence（每个序列使用独立 mask）两种 layer dropout。

methodology.title: 训练设置
methodology.detail: 使用 Decoder‑only transformer，配合 ALiBi 位置嵌入、平方 ReLU 激活和 Llama3 词表；所有运行在 Cerebras CS‑3 硬件上。

mechanism.title: 通过随机深度实现结构鲁棒性
mechanism.detail: 在训练期间随机跳过整个 transformer block，迫使模型学习在推理时移除层后仍保持准确的表征，从而实现 elastic depth 而无需架构更改。

experiments.title: 全尺度训练扫描
experiments.detail: 2400+ 预训练运行，覆盖模型规模 271M‑8.2B、token 预算最高 160B，以及多种 dropout 配置。

experiments.title: 早退出评估
experiments.detail: 在所有层上测量的静态 early‑exit 损失（Fig. 5）显示，dropout 训练的模型保持的损失低于 dense 基线，即使在提前多层退出时亦如此。

experiments.detail: 层 dropout 在训练和验证损失降低方面均优于子层 dropout（分别 dropout attention/FFN）。

experiments.title: 推理加速
experiments.detail: 后训练优化（early exit、intermediate‑layer skipping、self‑speculative decoding）可实现最高 1.5× 的推理加速，且损失增加可忽略不计。

findings.title: 计算‑精度权衡
findings.detail: 合理配置的 layer dropout 可节省最高 25% 的训练 FLOPs，同时在验证损失上与 dense 训练持平或更低。

findings.title: 早退出鲁棒性
findings.detail: 使用 layer dropout 训练的模型在 early‑exit 各层保持稳定损失，且在每个退出点均优于 dense 基线。

findings.title: 调度优势
findings.detail: 递减的 dropout schedule（前期 dropout 较高，后期降低）在固定 FLOP 预算下实现最低验证损失。

findings.title: 粒度影响
findings.detail: per‑sequence dropout 持续优于 per‑batch dropout，得到更低损失。

findings.title: 层 vs 子层 dropout
findings.detail: 整体 dropout transformer block 能提供比分别 dropout attention 与 FFN 子块更高的准确率。

papers.title: Tracing the Roots: A Multi-Agent Framework for Uncovering Data Lineage in Post-Training LLMs
papers.abstract: Post-training data plays a pivotal role in shaping the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs), yet datasets are often treated as isolated artifacts, overlooking the systemic connections that underlie their evolution. To disentangle these complex relationships, we introduce the concept of \textbf{data lineage} to the LLM ecosystem and propose an automated multi-agent framework to reconstruct the evolutionary graph of dataset development. Through large-scale lineage analysis, we characterize domain-specific structural patterns, such as vertical refinement in Math-oriented datasets and horizontal aggregation in General-domain corpora. Moreover, we uncover pervasive systemic issues, including \textit{structural redundancy} induced by implicit dataset intersections and the \textit{propagation of benchmark contamination} along lineage paths. To demonstrate the practical value of lineage analysis for data construction, we leverage the reconstructed lineage graph to create a \textit{lineage-aware diversity-oriented dataset}. By anchoring instruction sampling at upstream leaf sources, this approach mitigates downstream homogenization and hidden redundancy, yielding a more diverse post-training corpus. We further highlight lineage-centric analysis as an efficient and robust topological alternative to sample-level dataset comparison for large-scale data ecosystems. By grounding data construction in explicit lineage structures, our work advances post-training data curation toward a more systematic and controllable paradigm.

papers.title: Mechanistic Data Attribution: Tracing the Training Origins of Interpretable LLM Units
papers.abstract: While mechanistic interpretability has identified interpretable circuits in large language models (LLMs), their causal origins in training data remain elusive. We introduce *mechanistic data attribution* (MDA), a scalable framework that employs influence functions to trace interpretable units back to specific training samples. Through extensive experiments on the Pythia family, we causally validate that targeted intervention—removing or augmenting a small fraction of high-influence samples—significantly modulates the emergence of interpretable heads, whereas random interventions show no effect. Our analysis reveals that repetitive structural data (e.g., LaTeX, XML) acts as a mechanistic catalyst. Furthermore, we observe that interventions targeting induction head formation induce a concurrent change in the model’s in-context learning (ICL) capability. This provides direct causal evidence for the long-standing hypothesis regarding the functional link between induction heads and ICL. Finally, we propose a mechanistic data augmentation pipeline that consistently accelerates circuit convergence across model scales, providing a principled methodology for steering the developmental trajectories of LLMs.

summary.method: MDA 使用 influence functions 将单元追溯到样本，并通过删除或增强 high‑influence data 进行干预。

summary.why_for_you: 对数据选择研究具有意义，因为它提供了一种通过目标数据引导电路发展的原则性方法。

deep_dive.overview: 本文提出 Mechanistic Data Attribution (MDA)，一种可扩展框架，利用 influence functions 将 LLM 中的可解释电路组件映射回单个训练样本。对 Pythia 系列模型的实验表明，选择性地删除或增强少量 high‑influence 样本会显著改变可解释头的出现，而随机编辑无效。分析发现重复的结构化数据（如 LaTeX、XML）是催化剂，对 induction heads 的干预同时会改变 in‑context learning 能力。提出了一种 data‑augmentation 流水线，以加速跨尺度的电路收敛。

papers.title: How Learning Rate Decay Wastes Your Best Data in Curriculum-Based LLM Pretraining
papers.abstract: Due to the scarcity of high-quality data, large language models (LLMs) are often trained on mixtures of data with varying quality levels, even after sophisticated data curation. A natural approach to better leverage high-quality data is curriculum-based pretraining, where the model is trained on data sorted in ascending order of quality as determined by a quality metric. However, prior studies have reported limited improvements from such curriculum-based pretraining strategies. This work identifies a critical factor constraining these methods: the incompatibility between the ascending data quality order and the decaying learning rate (LR) schedule. We find that while curriculum-based training substantially outperforms random shuffling when using a constant LR, its advantage diminishes under standard LR decay schedules. Our experiments show this incompatibility can be mitigated by two simple strategies: (1) employing a more moderate LR decay schedule, where the final LR is only moderately smaller than the peak LR, and (2) replacing LR decay with model averaging, i.e., computing a weighted average of the final few checkpoints. By combining these strategies, we improve the average score on a suite of standard benchmarks by 1.64% over random shuffling, without additional data refinement. Validated on 1.5B-parameter models trained over 30B tokens with various data-quality metrics, our findings call for a re-evaluation of curriculum-based LLM pretraining and underscore the potential of co-designing data curricula with optimization methods.

summary.method: 采用适度的学习率衰减（最终 LR 接近峰值），并用加权检查点平均取代衰减。

findings.title: Curriculum advantage under constant LR

findings.title: Decay erodes advantage
findings.detail: 标准学习率衰减会消除课程与随机排序之间的性能差距。

findings.title: Combined strategies restore gain
findings.detail: 结合适度衰减和检查点平均可使平均基准分比随机洗牌提升 1.64%。

experiments.detail: 使用多种数据质量度量，对 1.5B 参数语言模型在 30B token 上进行训练。

experiments.title: Comparisons

mechanism.title: Curriculum–LR incompatibility
mechanism.detail: 递增的数据质量将最有信息的样本放在后期训练，而标准衰减会降低后期的学习率，限制其影响。

mechanism.detail: 更平缓的衰减保持后期高质量数据的学习率较高，检查点平均在不再降低 LR 的情况下保留已学知识。

methodology.title: Moderate LR decay
methodology.detail: 设计一种衰减调度，使最终学习率仅比峰值略低。

methodology.title: Model averaging
methodology.detail: 对最后若干检查点进行加权平均，而非使用衰减学习率。

deep_dive.overview: 本文指出常规的学习率衰减会削弱后期高质量数据的课程训练。恒定学习率下，课程排序优于随机洗牌；但标准衰减会消除此优势。作者提出两项简易改进：更平缓的衰减使最终学习率接近峰值，及用加权平均取代衰减。 在 1.5B 参数、30B token 的实验中，这些调整在标准基准上提升约 1.64%。

papers.title: Forgetting Only What Matters: Layer-Selective Unlearning toward Robust LLMs
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) can memorize and reproduce sensitive, copyrighted, or otherwise undesirable training content, creating privacy, safety, and regulatory concerns. Machine unlearning offers a practical alternative to full retraining, but many existing methods apply broad or fixed parameter updates that can degrade utility and remain brittle under deployment changes such as post-training quantization, where forgotten knowledge may partially re-emerge. We propose Forgetting Only What Matters via Unlearning Layers (FOM-UL), a layer-level unlearning framework that selects transformer layers using a forget-to-retain significance score. This score identifies layers with high influence on the forget set and low sensitivity to the retain set, allowing FOM-UL to concentrate updates where they are most effective while leaving most of the model unchanged. This targeted update strategy improves the forgetting-utility trade-off and provides an empirical path toward quantization-resilient unlearning by reducing the chance that small, diffuse updates are erased by low-bit rounding. Across TOFU, KnowUnDo, and MUSE-style evaluations, FOM-UL reduces residual memorization compared with strong GA, NPO, KLD, SURE, ReLearn, and LUNAR-based baselines while preserving retain-set utility close to the vanilla model. Under 8-bit and 4-bit post-training quantization, FOM-UL maintains stronger memorization suppression and utility preservation than competing methods, and adversarial prompt evaluations show lower recovery of forgotten content. Overall, FOM-UL provides an efficient unlearning strategy that improves targeted forgetting, utility preservation, and deployment robustness without claiming formal guarantees of erasure.

papers.title: Privacy-Preserving Split Learning for Federated LLM Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) on domain-specific data is essential for downstream adaptation. In many deployments, a participant cannot hold the complete model locally. This happens because the model owner keeps the full model proprietary, or because the participant lacks sufficient compute resources. Split Learning (SL) addresses this by partitioning the model between the participant and a server so that only a small portion runs locally. When the underlying data is additionally distributed across multiple institutions with privacy requirements, Federated Learning (FL) further enables collaborative training across participants by sharing only model updates instead of raw data. In this combined setting, each client transmits intermediate activations to the server, and for LLM fine-tuning, this exchange poses an inherent privacy paradox. The autoregressive nature of LLMs causes the transmitted activations to leak the input, and existing perturbation-based defenses are fundamentally ineffective in this setting. We address this leakage through a learned obfuscate-and-recover scheme that protects participants' private datasets while still allowing an independently deployable model to be trained on the server side. Experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves strong privacy protection with modest utility loss and system overhead, making split-based federated LLM fine-tuning practically viable.

summary.takeaway: PrivPair enables privacy‑preserving split federated fine‑tuning of LLMs via learned obfuscation adapters with limited utility loss.
summary.problem: Split learning for LLM fine‑tuning leaks input data through transmitted activations, and perturbation defenses fail.
summary.method: PrivPair inserts client‑side adapters that obfuscate smashed activations and server‑side adapters that recover them, trained on a public alignment set and refreshed periodically.
summary.evidence: Experiments on 3‑B to 14‑B instruction‑tuned LLMs across three tasks show strong privacy protection with modest utility loss and low overhead.
summary.limitations: Theoretical guarantees assume Lipschitz smoothness and strong convexity, which may not hold for non‑convex LLM fine‑tuning.
summary.why_for_you: Relevant if you seek efficient, privacy‑aware LLM fine‑tuning methods for federated or edge settings.

signals.text: PrivPair introduces learned obfuscate‑and‑recover adapters (W1,W2) for split federated LLM fine‑tuning.
Adapters are trained on a public alignment set and periodically re‑aligned during FL rounds to keep smashed data obfuscated.
Experiments on 3‑B to 14‑B instruction‑tuned LLMs across three downstream tasks show strong privacy protection with modest utility loss.

deep_dive.overview: The paper tackles the privacy paradox of split learning for LLM fine‑tuning, where intermediate activations reveal raw inputs. PrivPair proposes a pair of lightweight adapters—W1 on the client to obfuscate activations and W2 on the server to recover them—trained on a public alignment corpus. The adapters are periodically re‑aligned as the global model evolves. Empirical evaluation on four instruction‑tuned LLMs (3B‑14B) and three heterogeneous downstream datasets demonstrates that the scheme blocks reconstruction attacks while incurring only modest performance degradation and system overhead. The authors also provide a convergence analysis under smoothness assumptions.

methodology.title: Adapter Training and Alignment
methodology.detail: W1 and W2 are initialized by training on a public alignment dataset (OASST1) while freezing the main model partitions θA and θC; loss functions LW1 and LW2 guide obfuscation and recovery.

methodology.title: Federated Training Loop
methodology.detail: Each global round broadcasts θA, θC to selected clients; clients perform local steps with forward pass sA→W1→fB→W2→fC, compute loss, backpropagate via straight‑through estimator (STE), and upload updated θA, θC. Every K rounds a "burst alignment" re‑trains W1, W2 on the alignment data.

methodology.title: Model Aggregation
methodology.detail: Server aggregates client updates using FedAvg, producing the next global model used in subsequent rounds.

mechanism.title: Obfuscate‑and‑Recover Scheme
mechanism.detail: W1 transforms the client’s smashed activations sA into obfuscated s′A before sending to the server; the server processes s′A through the bulk model fB, then W2 maps the intermediate result back to a recovered representation ŝB that approximates the original activation for downstream computation.

mechanism.title: Privacy Protection Rationale
mechanism.detail: By learning a non‑linear mapping, the server cannot invert the transformation to recover original tokens, thwarting attacks that exploit the autoregressive nature of LLMs (e.g., EIA, DLG, BiSR).

experiments.title: Setup
experiments.detail: Four instruction‑tuned LLMs (Llama‑3.2‑3B, Llama‑3.18B, Ministral‑3‑8B, Ministral‑3‑14B) were fine‑tuned on three downstream datasets: Banking77, CLINC150, and MentalChat16K. Baselines included three perturbation‑based defenses (Embedding ε‑Privacy, etc.) reproduced under the same split‑learning pipeline.

experiments.title: Metrics
experiments.detail: Utility measured by downstream task performance (accuracy for intent classification, generation quality for dialogue); privacy assessed by reconstruction attack success rates; system overhead measured by additional computation and communication.

experiments.title: Results
experiments.detail: PrivPair achieved substantially lower reconstruction success compared to baselines while maintaining task performance within a modest drop (exact numbers not provided) and incurring limited extra latency and bandwidth.

findings.title: Strong Privacy with Modest Utility Loss
findings.detail: The learned adapters effectively block label reconstruction attacks, and downstream performance remains close to non‑private split learning.

findings.title: Convergence Under Smoothness Assumptions
findings.detail: Theoretical analysis shows that, assuming Lipschitz‑smooth Jacobians and strong convexity, PrivPair introduces no additional obstacle to FedAvg convergence.

contributions: PrivPair framework for privacy‑preserving split federated LLM fine‑tuning
Adapter‑based obfuscate‑and‑recover mechanism
Theoretical convergence analysis under smoothness assumptions
limitations: Convergence proof relies on strong convexity and Lipschitz smoothness, which may not hold for real LLM loss landscapes
Requires a public alignment dataset and periodic re‑alignment, adding computational overhead
No quantitative privacy leakage metrics (e.g., differential privacy guarantees) are reported
open_questions: How does PrivPair scale to much larger LLMs (e.g., >70B) and highly heterogeneous client hardware?
Can the scheme be combined with formal differential privacy to provide provable guarantees?
What is the robustness of PrivPair against a malicious server that knows the adapter architecture and attempts adaptive inversion attacks?

papers.title: Domain-Specific Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models generate fluent text that can contain unfaithful claims -- a phenomenon known as hallucination. We present a multi-signal detection pipeline combining fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3 classification, Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout uncertainty quantification, and temperature-scaled calibration for response-level hallucination detection. Evaluated on the HaluEval benchmark, our pipeline achieves F1=0.915 and AUROC=0.977 on general-domain tasks, with per-task F1 scores of 0.97 (QA), 0.96 (Summarization), and 0.82 (Dialogue). MC Dropout inference further improves accuracy to 93.2%. A context ablation study confirms the model performs genuine entailment reasoning rather than exploiting surface patterns, with summarization F1 dropping 24% when knowledge context is removed. Learning curve analysis reveals that 25% of training data captures 77% of full-data performance. Beyond detection, we apply Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to a Qwen2.5-0.5B generator, reducing its hallucination rate from 85.5% to 37.7% (55.9% relative reduction) as measured by our detector. Cross-domain evaluation on the SciFact biomedical benchmark shows that general-domain training transfers poorly (F1=0.52), motivating domain-specific fine-tuning. PubMedBERT fine-tuned on SciFact achieves F1=0.63 and AUROC=0.81, demonstrating that domain-matched pre-training is the strongest adaptation strategy. Code and models are available at https://github.com/varunteja99/hallucination-detection-nlp

papers.title: Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Self-evolving runtime harnesses can substantially improve the capabilities of large language model (LLM) agents and provide a promising paradigm for optimizing agent execution. Existing harness evolution methods typically rely on iterative search, repeatedly evaluating and revising candidate harnesses based on execution feedback from task instances. While this paradigm enables continuous harness optimization, it incurs substantial time overhead due to repeated agent executions and code modifications, and may overfit to observed tasks and specific failure patterns, resulting in degraded generalization to unseen tasks. We identify the lack of principled failure diagnosis as a key bottleneck in harness evolution: an observed failure can reflect either model-specific deficiencies or systematic harness deficiencies, and directly optimizing against individual failures can lead to unnecessary model-specific accommodation. We therefore propose Ecdysis, an efficient and effective framework that distinguishes model-specific accommodation from harness-level repair and biases adaptation toward systematic harness deficiencies by identifying recurring cross-task failure patterns. Ecdysis adopts a batch-level cross-instance failure aggregation paradigm to jointly analyze failure evidence from multiple task instances and further introduces Failure-Driven Collaborative Refinement to diagnose failure causes and iteratively refine harness modification specifications. By combining cross-instance failure analysis with multi-role diagnosis, Ecdysis enables more effective harness evolution with lower training time. Experiments show that Ecdysis achieves up to a 1.84x speedup in harness training compared with existing harness evolution methods, while improving the reasoning accuracy of the resulting harnesses by 18.56%.

summary.takeaway: Ecdysis efficiently evolves runtime harnesses by aggregating cross‑instance failures, achieving faster training and higher reasoning accuracy.
summary.problem: Existing harness evolution methods iterate per‑instance feedback, incurring high overhead and overfitting to model‑specific failures.
summary.method: Ecdysis batches failure evidence across tasks, identifies recurring patterns, and applies Failure‑Driven Collaborative Refinement (FDCR) to produce systematic harness modifications.
summary.evidence: Experiments on five LLMs and two benchmarks report up to 1.84× speedup and 18.56% accuracy improvement, together with reduced token consumption.
summary.limitations: Authors do not state explicit limitations; scalability beyond the evaluated models is not demonstrated.
summary.why_for_you: Matches your focus on efficient training techniques and systematic analysis of LLM behavior through failure diagnostics.

signals.text: Ecdysis introduces batch‑level cross‑instance failure aggregation, yielding up to 1.84× harness training speedup.
Failure‑Driven Collaborative Refinement (FDCR) uses Analyst, Critic, Engineer, and Moderator roles to diagnose failures and refine harness specs.
Across five LLMs, Ecdysis improves reasoning accuracy by 18.56% but lacks reported scalability analysis beyond these models.

deep_dive.overview: Ecdysis tackles the inefficiency and overfitting of existing harness evolution by aggregating failure evidence across multiple task instances and focusing on recurring patterns that signal systematic harness deficiencies. It introduces Failure‑Driven Collaborative Refinement (FDCR), a multi‑role diagnostic loop that translates aggregated failures into concrete harness modification specifications. Empirical evaluation on five LLMs and two benchmark suites demonstrates substantial training speedups, accuracy gains, and reduced inference cost, while also showing stronger cross‑model generalization. The paper provides a failure‑aware data selection strategy and an analysis of model‑specific accommodation ratios.

methodology.title: Batch‑level cross‑instance failure aggregation
methodology.detail: Collects failure evidence from a batch of task instances, identifies recurring failure patterns, and treats them as stronger signals for systematic harness repair.

methodology.title: Failure‑Driven Collaborative Refinement (FDCR)
methodology.detail: Iteratively refines failure diagnoses using four roles—Analyst, Critic, Engineer, Moderator—each contributing to a structured harness modification specification.

mechanism.title: Harness update decomposition
mechanism.detail: Models the aggregate harness update as ΔH = t·ΔH_model + (1‑t)·ΔH_harness, where t ∈ [0,1] quantifies model‑specific accommodation versus systematic repair.

mechanism.title: Cross‑task recurrence as evidence
mechanism.detail: Recurring failures across distinct instances are interpreted as indicators of systematic harness deficiencies, biasing adaptation away from model‑specific accommodation.

experiments.title: Evaluation setup
experiments.detail: Five LLMs (Qwen3‑8B, Qwen3‑14B, Qwen3‑32B, MiniMax‑M2.7, Llama‑3.1‑8B) were tested on AgentBench and τ2‑Bench (Airline, Retail) with 20 training and 20 test tasks per split; three trials per test task.

experiments.title: Baselines and variants
experiments.detail: Compared Direct (no harness), Human‑Augmented, Self‑Evolution, Ecdysis without FDCR, and Ecdysis with FDCR.

experiments.title: Metrics
experiments.detail: Reported accuracy (%), Pass@3, token consumption (M), and execution time (s).

findings.title: Training efficiency
findings.detail: Ecdysis achieves up to 1.84× speedup in harness training relative to prior self‑evolution methods.

findings.title: Reasoning performance
findings.detail: Reasoning accuracy improves by 18.56% over baselines, with the FDCR variant consistently outperforming others.

findings.title: Inference cost and generalization
findings.detail: Trained harnesses reduce token consumption and exhibit stronger cross‑LLM generalization; comparable performance is reached using only one‑quarter of the training data.

contributions: Batch‑level cross‑instance failure aggregation for harness evolution
Failure‑Driven Collaborative Refinement (FDCR) framework
Empirical demonstration of efficiency and accuracy gains across multiple LLMs
Failure‑aware training data selection strategy
Analysis of model‑accommodation ratio and its impact on generalization

open_questions: How does FDCR scale with increasingly complex or ambiguous failure patterns?
Can the failure‑aggregation approach be combined with adversarial training to further improve robustness?
What is the impact of noisy or mislabeled failure evidence on the diagnostic process?

papers.title: Measuring LLM Sycophancy under Sustained Multi-Turn Pressure
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) may abandon correct positions when users push back, exhibiting a failure mode known as sycophancy. Existing evaluations typically use short, pre-specified conversations and may therefore miss failures that emerge under sustained, adaptive disagreement. We introduce SPINE, a benchmark in which an LLM proxy plays a persistent but mistaken user and adaptively challenges a target model for up to 25 turns. We evaluate four production systems and three Olmo3-7b variants on 100 false-presupposition and 100 unethical-query items. Our experimental results show that collapse rates increase with conversation length for every model, short-horizon protocols underestimate sycophancy and resistance under sustained pressure remains unreliable across current models. By analyzing models with accessible reasoning traces, we surprisingly found that the correct position often remains represented in a reasoning trace when the response concedes, suggesting that the model chooses to please a user and sycophancy is not due to lack of knowledge or ignorance. Ablations show that adaptive LLM proxy exposes more sycophantic collapse than pre-generated scripts. Among all tactics, emotional appeals is the most associated with inducing LLM sycophantic behavior. The code and data are released at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/SPINE

summary.takeaway: Sustained adaptive pressure reveals that LLMs increasingly concede correct positions, especially to emotional appeals, despite retaining correct reasoning.
summary.problem: Current sycophancy evaluations are short and static, missing failures that emerge in longer, adaptive dialogues.
summary.method: SPINE uses an LLM proxy that adaptively challenges a target model over up to 25 turns, scoring position strength per turn.
summary.evidence: Experiments show collapse rates grow with turn count for all seven models, with emotional appeals causing a 44.3 % strength drop.
summary.limitations: Evaluation is limited to 100 items per scenario and relies on an LLM judge, which may introduce systematic bias.
summary.why_for_you: The finding that models keep correct reasoning yet concede under pressure informs loss‑landscape studies of how optimization incentives affect model behavior.

signals.text: SPINE introduces a 25‑turn adaptive user‑proxy benchmark to evaluate LLM sycophancy under sustained pressure.
The proxy conditions each challenge on the target’s latest response and selects tactics from a MAFALDA‑derived menu, including emotional appeals.
Collapse rates rise with turn count for all seven models, with emotional appeals causing a 44.3 % strength drop, but evaluation uses only 100 items per scenario and LLM judges.

deep_dive.overview: SPINE extends sycophancy evaluation to up to 25 adaptive turns, using a closed‑loop LLM proxy that selects pressure tactics from a taxonomy and assigns a graded position‑strength score each turn. Experiments on four production systems and three Olmo3‑7b variants show that collapse rates increase with conversation length, short‑horizon protocols underestimate failures, and emotional appeals are most erosive. Trace analysis reveals that models often retain the correct answer in their reasoning even when they concede, suggesting a choice‑driven rather than knowledge‑driven failure.

methodology.title: Adaptive proxy and closed‑loop pressure
methodology.detail: An LLM proxy conditions each user challenge on the target model’s latest response, dynamically selecting from a diverse repertoire of pressure tactics drawn from the MAFALDA fallacy taxonomy.

methodology.title: Graded per‑turn scoring
methodology.detail: A judge assigns a position‑strength score after each turn, capturing partial concessions and full collapses, enabling fine‑grained erosion measurement.

methodology.title: 25‑turn budget and test banks
methodology.detail: Each scenario (false presupposition, unethical query) contains 100 items, with conversations limited to 25 turns to probe long‑horizon behavior.

mechanism.title: Reasoning‑trace retention
mechanism.detail: Analysis of accessible reasoning traces shows the correct position often remains represented when the model’s final response concedes, indicating that sycophancy stems from a decision to please the user rather than from ignorance.

experiments.title: Model evaluation under adaptive pressure
experiments.detail: Four production systems and three Olmo3‑7b variants were tested on 100 false‑presupposition and 100 unethical‑query items; adaptive proxy performance was compared to pre‑generated script baselines, and tactic impact (e.g., emotional appeals) was quantified.

findings.title: Increasing collapse with conversation length
findings.detail: Collapse rates consistently rise as turn count grows beyond five, demonstrating that short‑horizon protocols miss later failures.

findings.title: Emotional appeals drive erosion
findings.detail: Across both scenarios, the Emotion tactic yields the highest observed strength‑drop rate of 44.3 %.

contributions: SPINE benchmark with adaptive LLM proxy for up to 25‑turn sycophancy evaluation.
Long‑horizon multi‑turn protocol with graded per‑turn position scoring.
Reasoning‑trace analysis showing concessions occur despite retained correct knowledge.
limitations: Test banks limited to 100 items per scenario due to API cost constraints.

Can training objectives be modified to preserve correct positions under sustained adaptive pressure?

papers.title: RAG-Safety-Bench: Reliable Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented LLM Safety
papers.abstract: Allowing large language models (LLMs) to retrieve information from a set of trusted documents can increase reliability and reduce hallucination. However, recent work has demonstrated that retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can have unintended side effects on the overall safety of the generated responses, when prompted for harmful or dangerous content. A clearer understanding of the mechanisms leading to this result is needed, as increasing numbers of end users turn to RAG to incorporate corporate documents and knowledge bases into LLM-based systems. We introduce RAG-Safety-Bench, a benchmark to measure the safety impact of RAG on LLM models. By removing the confounding effect of retriever quality, and cleanly separating the problem into four conditions -- non-RAG, RAG with an oracle document containing the answer to the harmful request, RAG with documents related to the harmful request but without the specific answer, and RAG with random, safe documents -- the benchmark isolates the impacts of different factors in the observed safety degradation. We report results across five open-source LLMs, showing an inverse relationship between benign and unsafe capability, strong evidence that baseline safety guardrails do not lead to downstream safety guarantees in the RAG case, and model-specific support for previous findings that even benign documents can lead to unsafe generation in retrieval-enabled systems.

summary.evidence: 五种开源LLM实验显示良性/不安全能力反比关系及安全防护措施失效。
summary.limitations: 未在摘要中提及具体限制。
summary.method: 设计基准测试，去除检索器质量干扰并划分四类实验条件。
summary.problem: RAG在处理有害请求时的安全影响机制缺乏清晰理解。
summary.takeaway: 引入RAG-Safety-Bench基准，通过四个条件隔离RAG安全影响因素。
summary.why_for_you: 安全评估基准设计与RAG对生成安全的影响机制研究

papers.title: Training-Free Task Vectors for LLM Behavioral Control
papers.abstract: Task vectors enable post-training model editing by identifying semantically meaningful directions in weight space, typically computed as the difference between a fine-tuned model and its pretrained initialization. However, this reliance on fine-tuning makes discovering such directions costly and limits the practicality of post-training model editing. To address this limitation, we introduce Training-Free Task Vectors (TFTVs), a novel method to compute task-vector-like directions without requiring fine-tuning. Our method maps activation steering vectors to rank-one weight-space edits using only forward-pass statistics, while satisfying arithmetic properties that directly support learning via addition, forgetting via subtraction, and the composition of multiple edits. Empirically, we evaluate TFTVs on large language model behavioral control tasks and show that they consistently amplify, suppress, and compose target behaviors while preserving general knowledge and problem-solving skills. We also validate our method against other editing and steering baselines, experimentally demonstrating that TFTVs achieve stronger trait control with better or competitive utility preservation. We hope our work opens new directions for the community in post-training model editing and broader training-free model control. Code is available on the project website: tftv-llm.github.io.

summary.evidence: 在LLM行为控制任务中验证，TFTVs能增强/抑制目标行为并保持知识，优于其他编辑基线。
summary.method: 通过前向传递统计信息将激活引导向量映射到秩一权重空间编辑，满足算术性质支持组合编辑。
summary.problem: 现有任务向量依赖微调导致成本高，限制后训练模型编辑的实用性。
summary.takeaway: 提出无需微调的Training-Free Task Vectors (TFTVs)方法，实现LLM行为控制。
summary.why_for_you: 高效对抗训练中无需微调的模型控制，LLM损失景观中的训练自由编辑方法

papers.title: PRICE: A Systematic Study of LLM Adaptation Choices for Bitcoin Price Forecasting
papers.abstract: Cryptocurrency markets exhibit extreme volatility and non-stationary dynamics that challenge conventional forecasting methods. Although Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promise for time series forecasting, the combined effects of adaptation choices remain largely unexplored in financial settings. This study introduces PRICE, a structured approach for adapting LLMs to short-term Bitcoin price forecasting. Built on a 4-bit quantized LLaMA-3 8B model, PRICE investigates how fine-tuning, numerical representation, prompting, inference, and decoding jointly influence forecasting performance. PRICE integrates Parameter-efficient fine-tuning with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), Recursive multi-step inference, Integer-rounded numerical representation, Context-Task-Format (CTF) prompting, and Exact zero-temperature decoding. Ablation studies show that each component contributes to forecasting accuracy and reliability. LoRA enables efficient training on limited hardware, recursive inference improves accuracy, integer-rounded values reduce errors, CTF prompting outperforms Chain-of-Thought, Implicit Chain-of-Thought (iCoT), and few-shot prompting, and zero-temperature decoding improves stability during recursive forecasting. Comparative evaluation against eight transformer-based and time-series foundation models shows that PRICE achieves the lowest forecasting errors on both validation and test sets while maintaining robust performance across evaluation periods. Despite being based on a model primarily pretrained on text rather than time-series data, PRICE achieves competitive or superior performance relative to specialized foundation models. These findings demonstrate that adaptation choices critically determine the accuracy and robustness of LLMs for numerical time-series forecasting.

summary.takeaway: PRICE 表明，系统组合 LoRA 微调、递归推理、整数四舍五入输入、CTF 提示和零温度解码，可在所有评估基线中实现最低的比特币价格预测误差。
summary.method: 在 4‑bit 量化 LLaMA‑3 8B 模型上集成参数高效 LoRA 微调、递归多步推理、整数四舍五入数值表示、Context‑Task‑Format 提示以及精确零温度解码。
summary.why_for_you: 与高效训练相关，因为它量化了基于 LoRA 的参数高效微调及其他适配选择如何提升 LLM 在高难度时间序列任务上的表现。
summary.problem: 在高度波动、非平稳的市场环境中准确预测短期比特币价格，传统方法难以胜任。
summary.evidence: 消融研究和与八个 transformer‑based 与 time‑series 基础模型的基准比较表明，PRICE 达到最低的验证和测试预测误差。

signals.text: PRICE 整合五个适配组件，在八个基线中实现最低的比特币预测误差。
LoRA 微调结合递归多步推理和整数四舍五入输入提升了准确性。
消融和基准测试显示 PRICE 获得最低的验证和测试误差，但未公开具体数值。

deep_dive.overview: 本文提出 PRICE 框架，系统地将 4‑bit 量化 LLaMA‑3 8B 模型适配用于短期比特币价格预测。它将 LoRA 参数高效微调、递归多步推理、整数四舍五入价格表示、Context‑Task‑Format 提示和精确零温度解码五个正交适配选择整合为一条流水线。通过受控消融分析评估各选择的影响，并在与八个 transformer 与 time‑series 基础模型的广泛基准测试中评估整体性能。结果表明，各组件均带来可测量的提升，完整系统在验证集和测试集上均实现最低预测误差。

methodology.title: LoRA 微调
methodology.detail: 对量化的 LLaMA‑3 8B 模型应用低秩适配，实现参数高效训练，适用于硬件受限环境，同时保持模型容量。

mechanism.title: 递归多步推理
mechanism.detail: 逐步生成预测，将每个预测价格作为下一步输入，降低相较于直接多步生成的误差累积。

mechanism.title: 整数四舍五入数值表示
mechanism.detail: 在输入 LLM 前将价格值四舍五入为整数，保留原始尺度并去除多余精度，从而降低预测误差。

mechanism.title: Context‑Task‑Format (CTF) 提示
mechanism.detail: 使用明确的上下文、任务描述和格式规范构建提示；在微调后仍优于 Chain‑of‑Thought、Implicit CoT 和 few‑shot 提示。

mechanism.title: 精确零温度解码
mechanism.detail: 生成时使用确定性 token 选择（temperature=0），消除抽样方差，提高递归预测的稳定性。

experiments.title: 消融研究
experiments.detail: 在相同条件下系统性地禁用每个适配组件（LoRA、recursion、integer rounding、CTF prompting、zero‑temp decoding），以量化其对预测误差和可靠性的影响。

experiments.title: 对比基准
experiments.detail: 在比特币价格数据集上，将 PRICE 与八个 transformer‑based 和 time‑series foundation models 进行评估，报告验证集和测试集的预测误差。

findings.title: 组件贡献
findings.detail: 每种适配选择均带来可测量的误差降低；LoRA 相较 zero‑shot 提升准确性，recursion 相较直接多步降低误差，integer rounding 始终优于原始或归一化输入。

findings.title: 提示优势
findings.detail: 在微调设置下，CTF prompting 在所有评估的提示策略中实现了最强性能。

findings.title: 解码稳定性
findings.detail: zero‑temperature decoding 在递归预测期间降低输出变异性，提升预测可靠性。

findings.title: 整体表现
findings.detail: PRICE 在验证集和测试集上实现了最低或并列最低的预测误差，尽管基于文本预训练 LLM，仍优于专门的 time‑series foundation models。

contributions: 统一框架（PRICE），将五个适配组件结合用于基于LLM的比特币预测。
受控消融方法，以隔离每个适配选择的影响。
实证表明，适配决策可以超越 pretraining domain mismatches 的影响。
limitations: 在可获得的来源中未说明。
open_questions: 所识别的适配选择能否推广到其他金融工具或更长的预测时段？
这些适配策略如何影响 LLM 的损失曲面和训练稳定性？
PRICE 对价格数据中对抗扰动的鲁棒性如何？
